blocks.text: 11-ADC / ad copy Goes here. A breakdown of Alex Hormozi's direct-response copywriting and ad creative frameworks. Covers specific ad creative types (e.g., B2B Case Study, "How to", Question hook), the CBO/spam testing methodology for creatives, and direct response design rules (FUD mitigation, benefit-driven headlines). Not here. • Technical setup of Shopify stores or basic theme customization -> 05-SET • Tracking, analytics, or attribution modeling -> 06-MEA

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details specific, actionable frameworks for generating high-performance ad copy and creatives, moving beyond generic advice to provide standardized prompt structures and design rules based on psychological principles and high-volume A/B testing. modules: [ADC] topics: [copywriting, ad creative, native ads, advertorials, CBO testing, spam testing, direct response design, visual hierarchy, FUD mitigation, value proposition] tier: 3 scope_hint: comprehensive

Topics. native ad strategy / defining the core purpose of a native image ad as bypassing ad blindness by breaking the user's scroll pattern and lowering psychological defenses with long-form storytelling; ad creative types / identifying three specific native ad formats: (1) The Question (e.g., "Can I ask a question?"), (2) The specific pain point/desire Case Study (e.g., $18k B2B grant), and (3) The B2C outcome story; spam testing methodology / detailing Alex Hormozi's approach of generating high quantities of distinct image variations (using different background colors, product placements, and text colors) to find a high-performing base asset through rapid testing; CBO creative testing / implementing a systematic creative testing process within a Campaign Budget Optimization (CBO) structure using 5-8 creatives and benefit-driven headlines to identify a statistical winner; standardized prompt engineering / utilizing structured, question-based prompts (e.g., "Who is this for?", "What are their FUDs?") to feed information to Claude for generating congruent direct-response ad copy; high-performance direct response design rules / listing five non-negotiable direct response design principles: (1) benefit-driven main headline ("who you are, what you do, what's in it for me"), (2) relevant hero image, (3) reduction of FUDs (Fear, Uncertainty, Doubt) beneath the call to action, (4) clear and visually differentiated Call to Action (CTA) button, and (5) benefit-driven sub-headlines ("the deeper why"); feature-to-benefit translation / requiring that all copy is written through the perspective of the customer by obsessively answering the question "what's in it for them?" at every section of the funnel.

Feature-to-Benefit Translation: A foundational copywriting rule that demands all features are translated into direct customer benefits by asking "what's in it for them?" multiple times to find the deepest "why."

The "So That" Method: A specific copywriting tactic used to drill down from a surface-level desire to the ultimate emotional driver (e.g., "Grow your revenue so that you can make more money so that you can retire your wife so that you can be happy").
Spam Testing creatives: The strategic high-volume testing of minor variations (colors, placement) on a winning ad creative base to rapidly maximize ROI.
CBO creative Testing Framework: A systematic direct-response testing process that uses broad targeting and value-based bidding to find winning ad assets with statistical significance.
Skip. The intro hook yapping about $350k in 30 days, specific product deep dives (like the grant list or grant writer examples), and repetitive plugs for joining the Social Brands Club 2.0.

Scope mix. 15% baseline (basic definitions of native ads and CTRs), 85% growth (advanced psychological frameworks, standardized prompting structures, and rigorous A/B testing methodologies). Volume. ~400 words.
